method.label: Bound using the lowest unit price

annotationRationale: The lowest unit price gives an upper bound valid for every purchase, and a legal purchase attains it. The supporting cost relationship is total price equals unit price times quantity.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official method: rule out fourteen popsicles using the cheapest unit price, then construct a purchase of thirteen.

review.mathCheck: Every allowed package costs at least $0.60 per popsicle, so any purchase of 14 or more costs at least $8.40. Two five-packs and one three-pack attain 13 for $8; choice D is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded adaptation of the first MAA solution #2 on page 2, preserving its universal unit-price bound and attaining purchase.
review.annotationCheck: The bound and construction satisfy both extremal criteria. The pricing relationship is appropriately supporting knowledge.
